claim_tested: Handoff §4.5 / invariant 14: maximum actual lots per LIVE LADDER EPISODE is 3, and fills above 3 per episode are zero in the cap3 arms.

source.note: Archived out of the repo for size; see reports/large-research-artifacts.json. This audit is a group-by over evidence that already existed — no campaign was rerun to produce it.

episode_definition: window | arm | kind | rep | tpr | tnr | horizon | ticker | entry. The replicate and skill coordinates belong in the key because the same ticker and entry date recur in every frontier cell; collapsing them would merge independent episodes and understate the maximum.

coverage.covers: W1 and W2, PERSISTENT and REDIAGNOSE arms: 64,081 live ladder episodes and 856,269 fills. Max lots per episode is 3 and fills above lot 3 are zero in EVERY cell, not just in aggregate.
does_not_cover: The monthly/lump contribution split. Handoff §4.5 states the claim for 'monthly/lump cap3 arms', but this ledger does not carry a regime/exposure dimension, so the audit cannot break the result out that way.
The THESIS_CAP3 arm. The ledger records arm values PERSISTENT and REDIAGNOSE only.
coverage.why_not_built_from_the_cap3_shards: The natural source would be reports/research/mechb/stage2-requirements/shard-*-cap3-*.json, but those record no per-episode fill instrumentation — their metrics stop at deployment and returns. Only the later uncapped-episode-exposure diagnostic added fills, max_fills_per_episode and actual_episode_fill_distribution. That asymmetry is the likely reason this audit never existed: the parent campaign never emitted the numbers it would have been built from.
coverage.corroborating_contrast: In the uncapped arm, with the same generator and the cap removed, actual_episode_fill_distribution reaches max 20 and max_fills_per_episode has a median of 14 (shard-W1-uncapped-lump.json). The cap is therefore the binding constraint here, not a coincidence of short episodes — without it, episodes routinely run far past three lots.
